To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have provided eigenvector-free solutions of the matrix equation AX + PX = B and XC + PXC = D with PX = PXP and XH sX constraints, which is a new result in the field of matrix equations with constraints.
we present eigenvector-free solutions for AX = B and XC = D under the constraints PX = QP and XH + sX = 0, where P is an involutory matrix.

we have presented the general solutions to the equations AX= B, XC = D, with PX = XP, XH = sX constraints, in terms of the Moore–Penrose inverse of the products generated from A, B, C and P, and the solutions are eigenvector-free.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the matrix equation AX × PX = B and the two matrix equations AX = BX and AX × CX = B with P × XP = P and X × XH = sX.
the matrix equations AX = BC, AX = BXC, XC = BC and AX = BDC with PX = sP and XH + sX = sI, where s = + 1 or −1, and the matrix P is a given nonsingular Hermitian involutive matrix.
the constrained matrix equations AX = sB, AX = sXB, AX = BXC, XC = AXC, AX = XBXC, AX = CXB, and XC = BXC with the constraints PX = XPP, XH = PX, XH + sXP = sPX + P, and XH + PX = sPX.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a general Hermitian involutary matrix P, the constrained matrix equations AX = BC, XC = DB and AX = XB, XC = B with P and XH + sXH constraints are solvable, where s = 1, 2, 4.
the constrained matrix equations can be solved without using any eigenvectors.
the eigenvector-free representations are available for all the above-mentioned equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a unified treatment for the matrix equations AX = B and XC = D with the constraints PX = XP and XH + sX = 0.
the eigenvectors can always be avoided in solving the matrix equations with the involutory constraints.
we have provided eigenvector-free solutions for a class of matrix equations with Hermitian involutary constraint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the eigenvalue decomposition of a Hermitian involutary matrix is a powerful tool to release the eigenvectors in the solutions to the matrix equations with constraints.
the eigenvector-free solutions can be derived from the eigenvector solutions by applying the generalized inverses.
the eigenvalues of P can be used to determine the number of solutions to AX + BX = C with PX = sXP.
